title: Yet, Heard
essence: Three calls made at the edge of a harbour before leaving: to the lover under a shared moon, to the mother over a black hole that opens in the water, to the father who walks out of the eastern sky. One night on one quay, and the light is the clock: moon high, the dead hour, first grey, the sun coming up out of the harbour mouth. Each call is a dashed line of light strung between two people, and behind every call the same breakup keeps playing on the sidewalk.
palette_notes: Night navy and harbour teal from the bay stills (3238a164 lamps on black water, ef9f6c7e night quay); sodium amber of the quay lamps and the town across the water from the same two; neon red only in the club sidewalk opening (b05d5b9a puddle, 7fdacba9 street); the moon is paper cream, never pure white. Dawn walks the sky from slate grey (#8a8f9a) to sunrise apricot (#f2b35a) in M3-M4. Electric blue (#2f6bff) is the poem's single accent: 'someone blue', one point of light on the poet's chest in the last few seconds, nowhere else.

full_text.line: Accepting you'll never say nor ever feel, my love was real.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
I gather my things to go.
Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it
and settle down the stillnessism.
We talk for years and travel through time
and it feels so good.
We grow old together.
I believe maybe we could have it all,
or swing in my humbled late nights and heartbreaks
and an end story unchanging.
You help me gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my mother.
In tears, speaking of an abyss, she's never known.
And we talk for years and we closet wounds
and we explain my way of birth then and even after prayer.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
We grow old together with the moon looking at us
the way we used to be.
As my tears fall between the creases and faith,
dancing on my own, maternal ears in tune.
She watches us gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my father.
Summon his calming demeanor from the yonders
and we walk for years and travel east toward the sunrises
and retrace his footsteps now and then.
Guiding a settling down moon the way it used to leave
and my tears fall between the creases
and wave shadows of the inner harbor.
We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken.
Someone borrowed and someone blew.
Yet broken, yet hurt.

arc.beat: out of the club, through a fawning crowd, he glimpses EX's back and cannot reach him; then the two of them walk the waterfront and look up at the same moon while the years pass as moonlight
arc.image: two backs on the quay lip, heads tipped up at one paper moon, each with his own road of light on the water opening into a V

arc.beat: suitcases on the sidewalk; he calls his mother from a lit booth while the breakup plays behind him; she weeps and the harbour between them goes bottomless
arc.image: the call-cord sagging into a black hole cut in the water, tears peeling off the cord and falling into nothing

arc.beat: he hangs up, the mother dissolves; he dials again and the father resolves out of the paling east; they walk the quay east, the son stepping into prints already worn in the stone
arc.image: a dark footprint trail on wet stone pointing east under the first grey

arc.beat: father and son stroll into the sunrise, one brief shake on 'shaken'; back at the booth EX turns to haze and is gone; the poet stands alone in first sun
arc.image: a half sun sitting in the harbour mouth, harbour lights going out, one blue point on the poet's chest

best_footage.element: lamps reflected as broken vertical streaks on black water under a quay wall and bridge piers; teal and sodium lamps alternating
best_footage.why: Exactly the world module's 'a light on water is a broken vertical streak'. Paint the streaks as a separate translucent card under the town lamps so they can be pulled out when the sun rises (harbor_lights_out).

best_footage.element: wet stone quay with lamp pools, low dark hill ridge across the water, a scatter of town lights at the waterline, starred navy sky
best_footage.why: The whole layer order of the harbour set in one frame: sky / far ridge with lights / water / quay stone. The stone's wet slabs are the floor card for the footprint trail of M3.

best_footage.element: a puddle mirroring red columns and blue neon signs down a long arcade
best_footage.why: The club sidewalk floor: a glossy black floor card with painted red/blue reflections reads as rain and nightlife without animating any rain. Only used in the opening 09.1a-b.

best_footage.element: rainy street with power lines, a lit corner shop, red and teal smears on wet asphalt
best_footage.why: The film cut already opens on it; the shopfront glow and overhead wires are the back layer of the club street before he reaches the water.

best_footage.element: a gibbous moon with clear maria on black
best_footage.why: Reference for the moon card: a cream disc with three small soft maria, not a lamp and not a face (the module rejected both).

best_footage.element: worm's-eye view up a canyon of towers to a single bright moon
best_footage.why: In the film cut. Gives the one upward insert for 'we look at the moon the way we used to see it': the poet's POV between buildings before we cut to the two backs on the quay.

best_footage.element: a red glass door glowing at the end of a dark blue alley, its light spilling on wet pavement
best_footage.why: How the phone booth should read: the only warm lit box on a cold street, light spilling out as a painted wedge on the pavement card.

best_footage.element: a lone figure at a railing above a teal, fogged city; a single red reflection on the wet deck
best_footage.why: The last shot (09.4d) and the quay-lip staging: one small dark figure against a huge toned field, rail as a single thin card.

best_footage.element: a concrete opening framing bright night water, a bench in the dark foreground
best_footage.why: Frame-within-frame for the mother's living room: her big window must show the harbour sidewalk where the breakup plays, brighter than the room.

best_footage.element: a woman with a full afro seen from behind on a waterfront boardwalk, watching the water
best_footage.why: MOTHER at the curb watching the breakup with the poet (09.2c): the woman puppet from behind, small against the water, before the cut to her face.

props.name: the lit phone booth
props.look: a glass street booth with a steel frame, a folding door, a lit ceiling panel and a steel wall phone; the only warm box on a cold quay
props.build: Three layered cards: a back panel with the wall phone, a clear acetate glass front with painted steel mullions and a folding door on two brads, a cream-yellow lit ceiling strip. A cut-out light wedge card lies on the pavement in front. Poet slides between back panel and acetate.

props.name: the call (the cord of light)
props.look: a dashed, pulsed line between two callers: paper-white against the night sky, ink-dark against the dawn; it bows up to the moon for the lover, sags into the water for the mother
props.build: Coded overlay (dash pattern stepped along the line) or, in camera, a strip of 5-on/2-off punched paper dashes on fine wire bent to the sag; two versions (cream and ink).

props.name: the moon
props.look: a cream paper disc with three small soft maria and a thin grey rim; the brightest thing in the film until the sun
props.build: Single card, cream with a fine grey ring; a second card for its road on the water (a broken vertical streak of paper flecks).

props.name: the sun in the harbour mouth
props.look: only the part of a disc above the waterline: a half sun sitting in the gap of the far shore. No still fits.
props.build: Half-disc card with a thin grey edge, slid up from behind the far-shore card through the gap; a warm wash card over the sky behind it.

insights: Build one harbour and relight it four times rather than four sets: the light is the clock (moon, dead hour, grey, sunrise).
The cord is the call. Keep it dashed and pulsing; it is the cheapest way to say 'on the phone' across a wide frame.
The breakup must keep playing in the background of every call: use a second, smaller POET + EX pair on a far layer, looped.
Dissolves are rationed: only the mother leaving, the father arriving and EX's haze. Every other change is a cut.
Aging must never be literal: years pass as the moon climbing.
Hold the blue accent back to the final seconds; it is the only time blue appears in the poem.
future: Harbour quay kit and the moon/sun discs return in 13 (the harbour) and the sunrise light feeds 11.
Elder FATHER walk cycle can be reused for the remembered elders in 12.
The dot-dissolve card technique carries to the ghost child and to 10's dawn sweep.
The poet's suitcase leaves with him; the empty sidewalk where 10 starts is this sidewalk at the end of the night.
